This reference is generated from the command dispatch and argparse definitions.
A bare `python -m agent <file>` invocation uses `heal` mode. The `mumei-heal`,
`mumei-extract-spec`, and `mumei-agent-mcp` console scripts map to `heal`,
`extract-spec`, and `mcp-server`, respectively.

`verify-foreign` is an alias of `validate-code`.

| `native-object-accept` | 7 | Run Core's bounded object-stage machine-code acceptance under an assumed, not validated, register convention and stated input domain. Core's machine_code_entry_wrapper_tv is consumed only when the valid descriptor lists it in checks_performed; when applicable, it checks one unconditional main call to __mumei_user_main returning the low 32 bits of its result. Applicability requires both object symbols and a supported __mumei_user_main source signature. This makes no CRT, loader, OS exit-status, ABI or runtime claim; os_exit_status_observation remains a separate runtime-observation check and is not discharged. This emits no evidence candidate, is not reusable Evidence or a certificate, is not a recovery performer, and does not promote a grade; broader C entry-wrapper behavior, CRT, loader/libc, ABI/runtime, optimizer semantics, producer authenticity and historical execution remain outside the profile. object_translation_correspondence here is only profile-bounded source-to-object machine-code correspondence, not universal object TV. Core's machine_code_f64_scalar_function_tv is consumed only when listed in checks_performed and is limited to Core's f64 profile with XMM argument/result registers assumed, not validated. MXCSR RNE, masked exceptions, FTZ/DAZ-off assumptions and NaN payload bits remain unestablished and not performed; the agent never discharges the external-callee, MXCSR or NaN-payload assumption markers even if a descriptor lists them as performed. Direct-call f64 arguments are admitted only under Core's exact-bits obligation (NaN-aware match, then an exact-bit proof against the XMM argument); computed f64 arguments without provably identical bits and f64 tail calls fail closed. This makes no IEEE-754 conformance, ABI, runtime or full object-TV claim. Core's `machine_code_composite_register_aggregate_tv` is consumed only when listed in `checks_performed`. It covers one- through sixteen-leaf struct parameters and direct-call struct arguments, and struct results of at most four leaves (at most three integer leaves in rax/rdx/rcx and at most two f64 leaves in xmm0/xmm1), with integer and/or f64 leaves; an i128/u128 leaf occupies two consecutive integer slots, low half first. Integer leaves take the next register in rdi–r9 and f64 leaves the next in xmm0–xmm7; leaves without a free register in their class are passed on the argument stack in declaration order, as LLVM lowers scalar stack arguments. Four-integer-leaf results (hidden sret) and three-f64-leaf results (x87) fail closed. One- and two-leaf values use Core's existing assumed SysV eightbyte convention; aggregates wider than two leaves assume LLVM first-class aggregate lowering, not SysV C-ABI classification, and `machine_code_tv_sysv_memory_class_aggregate_abi` stays not performed. This makes no ABI, runtime or full object-TV claim. |

## `mumei-agent forge`

Autonomous forge mode: extend the mumei std library with verified atoms from task specs.

### Options

| Option | Value | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--tasks-dir` | `<TASKS_DIR>` | no | forge_tasks/ | Directory containing forge task spec JSON files (default: forge_tasks/) |
| `--mumei-repo` | `<MUMEI_REPO>` | no | — | Path to the mumei repo (the one containing std/). Defaults to the MUMEI_REPO env var or the agent repo root. |
| `--max-tasks` | `<MAX_TASKS>` | no | — | Maximum number of tasks to execute (default: all) |
| `--task` | `<TASK>` | no | — | Run a single task spec file (looked up relative to --tasks-dir if not absolute) |
| `--dry-run` | — | no | — | Print the execution plan and exit without running anything |
| `--auto-commit, --no-auto-commit` | — | no | — | Override each task's auto_commit flag (--auto-commit to force on, --no-auto-commit to force off) |
| `--max-retries` | `<MAX_RETRIES>` | no | — | Override each task's max_retries |
| `--controls-gate` | `{off, warn, require}` | no | — | Negative-controls gate mode (default: CONTROLS_GATE or warn) |
| `--log-path` | `<LOG_PATH>` | no | — | Path to forge_log.json (default: <tasks_dir>/../forge_log.json) |
| `--harness-profile` | `{basic, stateful, verifier, self_evolution, lean_fallback, full}` | no | basic | NLAH module-ablation profile. Heavy multi-candidate search is enabled only by self_evolution/full. |
| `--benchmark-feedback` | `<BENCHMARK_FEEDBACK>` | no | — | Path to a mumei.benchmark_forge_feedback/v1 document from 'benchmarks/run_benchmarks.py --forge-feedback'. Biases task priorities toward the weakest benchmark categories' stdlib domains. |


## `mumei-agent propose`

Generate forge task specs from analyze_std_gaps output (SI-5 Phase 2-A).

Exactly one of `--gaps-json`, `--auto` is required.

### Options

| Option | Value | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--gaps-json` | `<GAPS_JSON>` | no | — | Path to a JSON file produced by analyze_std_gaps |
| `--auto` | — | no | — | Invoke analyze_std_gaps via the mumei MCP server in-process (requires the mumei repo on PYTHONPATH) |
| `--output-dir` | `<OUTPUT_DIR>` | no | forge_tasks | Directory to write generated spec files into (default: forge_tasks/) |
| `--overwrite` | — | no | — | Overwrite existing vstd_*.json files instead of writing a suffixed copy |
| `--dry-run` | — | no | — | Print the plan without writing any files |

### Options

| Option | Value | Required | Default | Description |

## `mumei-agent generate`

Generate verified Mumei code from a JSON specification

Exactly one of `--spec`, `--spec-file` is required.

### Options

| Option | Value | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--spec` | `<SPEC>` | no | — | Inline JSON specification string |
| `--spec-file` | `<SPEC_FILE>` | no | — | Path to a JSON specification file |
| `--output` | `<OUTPUT>` | yes | — | Output path for the generated .mm file |
| `--max-retries` | `<MAX_RETRIES>` | no | — | Maximum number of fix attempts (default: from config or 5) |
| `--metrics` | — | no | — | Output JSON metrics summary at the end |
| `--controls-gate` | `{off, warn, require}` | no | — | Negative-controls gate mode (default: CONTROLS_GATE or warn) |


## `mumei-agent proliferate`

Autonomous proliferation loop: analyze gaps → spec → generate → blast-radius check → heal → PR (SI-5 Phase 2-C).

### Options

| Option | Value | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--mumei-repo` | `<MUMEI_REPO>` | yes | — | Path to the mumei repository (must contain std/) |
| `--max-proposals` | `<MAX_PROPOSALS>` | no | 3 | Maximum number of proposals to process (default: 3) |
| `--mumei-bin` | `<MUMEI_BIN>` | no | — | Path to the mumei binary (default: MUMEI_BIN env or 'mumei') |
| `--dry-run` | — | no | — | Skip git/PR operations and do not persist generated files |
| `--output-json` | `<OUTPUT_JSON>` | no | — | Optional path to write a structured run summary as JSON (used by the SI-5 Phase 3-B scheduled workflow). |
| `--enable-lean-fallback` | — | no | True | Enabled by default: after forge + verify, hand any ``unknown`` atoms to mumei-lean's bridge.py for Lean 4 discharge. Requires MUMEI_LEAN_REPO to point at a mumei-lang/mumei-lean checkout. |
| `--disable-lean-fallback` | — | no | True | Disable Lean 4 fallback for local/debug runs. CI keeps the default enabled path. |
| `--enable-lean-ai-proof` | — | no | — | Task 2-D opt-in: after the Lean fallback, let the LLM write and auto-repair Lean 4 proofs for atoms that are still unknown; only proofs that pass 'lake build' are promoted to lean_verified. Skipped when no LLM key is configured or CI_FIXTURE_MODE is set. |
| `--enable-self-correction` | — | no | — | Run the structured-feedback self-correction loop when forge verification fails with structured feedback. |
| `--harness-profile` | `{basic, stateful, verifier, self_evolution, lean_fallback, full}` | no | basic | NLAH module-ablation profile. Heavy multi-candidate search is enabled only by self_evolution/full. |
| `--benchmark-feedback` | `<BENCHMARK_FEEDBACK>` | no | — | Path to a mumei.benchmark_forge_feedback/v1 document from 'benchmarks/run_benchmarks.py --forge-feedback'. Weak benchmark categories bias their stdlib domains forward in the queue. |
| `--parallel-forge-workers` | `<PARALLEL_FORGE_WORKERS>` | no | — | Maximum concurrent forge generations. Defaults to min(4, proposals) or PROLIFERATE_FORGE_WORKERS when set. |


## `mumei-agent harness-ablation`

Compare harness_metrics aggregates across --harness-profile runs against a baseline (module ablation report).

### Positional arguments

| Argument | Required | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runs` | yes | `<LABEL=SUMMARY_JSON> ...` | Run summary JSON files produced with --harness-profile, labelled as LABEL=path (e.g. full=out/full.json basic=out/basic.json). |

### Options

| Option | Value | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--baseline` | `<BASELINE>` | yes | — | Label of the baseline run to compare against. |
| `--format` | `{json, markdown}` | no | json | Report output format (default: json). |
| `--output` | `<OUTPUT>` | no | — | Write the report to this path instead of stdout. |

### Options

| Option | Value | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--code-file` | `<CODE_FILE>` | yes | — | Path to existing source code file or directory. |
| `--language` | `{python, rust, typescript, go, solidity}` | no | — | Source language. Inferred from the file extension when omitted. |
| `--json` | — | no | — | Output the full result as JSON. |
| `--format` | `{human, markdown, json, text}` | no | human | Output format (default: human). |
| `--output` | `<OUTPUT>` | no | — | Optional output path. |
| `--domain-hint` | `<DOMAIN_HINT>` | no | — | Optional domain hint for spec extraction. |
| `--auto-migrate` | — | no | — | Emit migration_hints by generating .mm migration skeletons for functions with issues. |
| `--auto-heal` | — | no | — | Run the self-healing loop on each skeleton produced by --auto-migrate. |
| `--heal-output-dir` | `<HEAL_OUTPUT_DIR>` | no | — | Directory to write healed .mm files (default: same directory as --code-file). |
| `--enable-lean-bridge` | — | no | — | Run the optional mumei-lean bridge for Solidity guard-trace certificates. |
| `--mumei-lean-repo` | `<MUMEI_LEAN_REPO>` | no | — | Path to the mumei-lean checkout used by --enable-lean-bridge. |
| `--enable-body-port` | — | no | — | Have the LLM port each function body to Mumei and verify it against the extracted contract; refuted ports count as code findings (needs an LLM). Sensitive environment values and credential-shaped literals are redacted from the source sent to the LLM and from the stored body, diagnostics and counterexamples; the redaction is pattern-based, so review code that holds unusual credentials before enabling it. |
| `--enable-native-replay` | — | no | — | Run each extracted Python, TypeScript, Go or Rust function natively on its counterexamples and a few boundary inputs, and check the extracted contract on the result; a violation is a confirmed code finding, and a refuted body port the native code does not reproduce is dropped. Executes the audited code locally. |
| `--include-tests` | — | no | — | Also audit test files (e.g. *_test.go, *.test.ts, test_*.py, tests/ dirs), which are skipped by default for directory audits. |
| `--enable-summaries` | — | no | — | Directory audits only: invoke each declared *-summaries produce route on the collected source units and record declared manifest metadata (route, unit, status, context key, function count) under summary_audits — advisory; manifest bytes are not stored. |
| `--summaries-manifest-map` | `<<PATH>>` | no | — | Directory audits only, requires --enable-summaries: JSON object mapping each unit label (as emitted under summary_audits) to a prior summary manifest. Units with a declared manifest run their *-summaries-reuse route and report mode/reused/derived counts; a stale or rejected manifest falls back to the produce route. With --enable-summary-attempts a mapped unit runs its *-summaries-reuse-attempt route instead. |
| `--enable-summary-attempts` | — | no | — | Directory audits only, requires --enable-summaries: run each summary unit through its declared <route>-attempt route and record the attempt report's acceptance envelope (mode/accepted/check_outcome/manifest_sha256) instead of manifest metadata — advisory; report bytes are not stored. With --summaries-manifest-map a mapped unit runs its *-summaries-reuse-attempt route (mode reuse-attempt); a stale manifest falls back to the plain -attempt route. |
| `--summary-attempt-timeout` | `<<MS>>` | no | 120000 | Declared attempt bound in milliseconds passed to each <route>-attempt unit (default: 120000). |
| `--enable-summary-plan` | — | no | — | Directory audits only, requires --enable-summaries: run the probe-boundary planner once per summary profile present among the collected units and record the advisory mumei.summaries-plan/v1 documents under summary_plans — routing only; no summary is derived. Planning executes each adapter's declared probe command. |
| `--summary-plan-stamp` | `<<N>>` | no | 1 | Host-declared observation stamp for the probe requests --enable-summary-plan records (default: 1). |
| `--summary-plan-tool-version` | `<<VERSION>>` | no | — | Optional declared tool version the --enable-summary-plan planner pins against. |
| `--summary-plan-histories` | `<<PATH>>` | no | — | Optional JSON array of persisted mumei.adapter-probe-history records the --enable-summary-plan planner resumes. |
| `--go-types` | `<<PATH>>` | no | — | Path to the provisioned tools/go-types helper binary; Go summary units record skipped_no_helper when --enable-summaries is set without it. |
| `--enable-scheduled-verification` | — | no | — | Dispatch each unit's generated .mm spec through run_attempt_schedule against the declared --schedule-request/--schedule-adapters/--schedule-argv-map/--schedule-policy inputs and record the mumei.attempt-schedule/v1 descriptor per unit. Dispatch record only — never a verdict. Requires the four declared input paths. |
| `--schedule-request` | `<<PATH>>` | no | — | Declared RouteRequirements JSON for --enable-scheduled-verification (source input contract required). |
| `--schedule-adapters` | `<<PATH>>` | no | — | Declared JSON array of adapter manifests for --enable-scheduled-verification. |
| `--schedule-argv-map` | `<<PATH>>` | no | — | Declared JSON object mapping adapter_id to its argv prefix for --enable-scheduled-verification; the unit's generated spec path is appended as the final argument. |
| `--schedule-policy` | `<<PATH>>` | no | — | Declared planner policy JSON for --enable-scheduled-verification; allowed_permissions must be declared. |
| `--schedule-observations` | `<<PATH>>` | no | — | Optional declared JSON array of runtime observations for --enable-scheduled-verification. |
| `--schedule-max-attempts` | `<<N>>` | no | — | Bounded schedule attempts per unit for --enable-scheduled-verification (default: 8). |
| `--schedule-success-exit-code` | `<<N>>` | no | — | Declared exit code counting as a scheduling success for --enable-scheduled-verification (repeatable; default {0}). |
| `--schedule-memory-bound-mb` | `<<MB>>` | no | — | Optional declared POSIX RLIMIT_AS ceiling per scheduled attempt child. |
| `--schedule-core` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Optional Core executable: when a scheduled verification selects an attempt, run the Core representation check on its captured output and record the mumei.evidence-check-acceptance/v1 descriptor on the schedule record; also record Core's schedule representation and consistency diagnostic under scheduled_verification_check (advisory only, not a verdict or Evidence acceptance). Use --json for the full record; text output shows the schedule outcome and check status. |
| `--schedule-core-requirement` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Optional mumei.evidence-requirement/v1 document: with --schedule-core, run the Core evidence-acceptance check (`core evidence accept --stdin --json --requirement PATH`) on the selected attempt's captured output instead of the representation check, and record Core's declared verdict as the evidence_check outcome. |
| `--schedule-core-requirement-list` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Optional mumei.evidence-requirement-list/v1 document: with --schedule-core, run the conjunctive Core evidence-acceptance check (`core evidence accept --stdin --json --requirement-list PATH`) on the selected attempt's captured output instead of the representation check, and record Core's declared verdict as the evidence_check outcome. Conflicts with --schedule-core-requirement. |


## `mumei-agent extract-spec`

| Option | Value | Required | Default | Description |

| `--text` | `<TEXT>` | no | — | Natural language requirement text |
| `--text-file` | `<TEXT_FILE>` | no | — | Path to a file containing natural language requirements |
| `--code-file` | `<CODE_FILE>` | no | — | Path to a source-code file or directory to convert into natural language requirements |
| `--code-language` | `{rust, c, go, python, javascript, typescript, java, cpp, solidity, unknown}` | no | — | Optional language override for --code-file |
| `--from-tests` | `<PATH> ...` | no | — | Check the extracted spec against harvested Python/Rust tests. |
| `--from-tests-language` | `{rust, python}` | no | — | Language override for --from-tests inputs. |
| `--observations-output` | `<OBSERVATIONS_OUTPUT>` | no | — | Write the final observation-check report to this JSON file. |
| `--domain` | `{financial, compliance, regtech, security, iot, web, data_structure, math, general}` | no | — | Optional domain hint for safer specification extraction |
| `--output` | `<OUTPUT>` | yes | — | Output path for the extracted forge task spec JSON |
| `--generate` | — | no | — | Generate and verify .mm code after extracting the spec |
| `--check-contradiction-only` | — | no | — | Extract specs and run only direct contradiction detection; skip code generation |
| `--generate-output` | `<GENERATE_OUTPUT>` | no | — | Output path for generated .mm code when --generate is set |
| `--max-retries` | `<MAX_RETRIES>` | no | 3 | Maximum spec extraction retry attempts |
| `--max-generation-retries` | `<MAX_GENERATION_RETRIES>` | no | — | Maximum code generation/self-healing retry attempts |
| `--max-refinements` | `<MAX_REFINEMENTS>` | no | 3 | Maximum spec refinement attempts when --generate is set |
| `--forge` | — | no | — | Write the extracted spec to forge_tasks/ and run the forge pipeline |
| `--forge-tasks-dir` | `<FORGE_TASKS_DIR>` | no | forge_tasks | Directory where --forge writes the extracted task spec |
| `--mumei-repo` | `<MUMEI_REPO>` | no | — | Path to the mumei repo used by --forge |
| `--forge-dry-run` | — | no | — | Preview the forge plan after extraction without generating code |
| `--forge-log-path` | `<FORGE_LOG_PATH>` | no | — | Path to forge_log.json when --forge runs |

| Option | Value | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--go-types` | `<<PATH>>` | yes | — | Path to the provisioned tools/go-types helper binary. |
| `--source` | `<<PATH>>` | yes | — | Go source file to summarize. Repeat for a multi-file package unit; each file is declared under its basename and basenames must be unique. |
| `--target-arch` | `{386, amd64, arm64}` | no | amd64 | Target architecture for gc sizes (default: amd64). |
| `--timeout` | `<<SECONDS>>` | no | 30 | Helper process timeout in seconds (default: 30). |
| `--import` | `<<IMPORT_PATH>=<FILE>>` | no | [] | Declare one source file of an importable package. Repeat per file and per import path; each path declares a package unit. Requires a multi-file --source package unit. |
| `--output` | `<<PATH>>` | no | — | Write the attempt report JSON here instead of stdout. |
| `--summary-aware-calls` | `<<MANIFEST>>` | no | — | Declared callee summary manifest (mumei.go-scalar-parameter-deps/v1): calls resolving to a callee it covers fold the declared return_dependencies and statement_reads instead of the opaque every-argument approximation. Advisory only — callees it misses keep opaque-call behavior. |
| `--attempt-timeout` | `<<MS>>` | yes | — | Declared attempt bound in milliseconds (required). The inner helper's own --timeout stays a separate bound. |
| `--memory-bound-mb` | `<<MB>>` | no | — | Optional declared POSIX RLIMIT_AS ceiling applied to the attempt child's whole address space. |

## `mumei-agent signature-eval`

Evaluate a declared producer-signature envelope and emit the representation-level evaluation.

### Options

| Option | Value | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--envelope` | `<PATH>` | yes | — | Declared producer-signature envelope JSON (mumei.producer-signature/v1). |
| `--expected-subject` | `<HEX>` | no | — | Declared record digest the signature should cover (64-char lowercase SHA-256 hex, e.g. an accepted descriptor's evidence_fingerprint). When supplied the evaluation emits subject_bound comparing it to the envelope's subject_digest. |
| `--expected-producer-key` | `<ID>` | no | — | Declared producer key fingerprint the caller trusts, arriving over a separately trusted channel. When supplied the evaluation emits key_pinned comparing it to the envelope's producer_key_id. |
| `--revocation-list` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Declared revocation list JSON (mumei.key-revocation-list/v1 or /v2) supplied over a separately trusted channel. When supplied the evaluation emits key_not_revoked checking the envelope's producer_key_id against the list's revoked_keys. |
| `--key-registry` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Declared producer-key registry JSON (mumei.producer-key-registry/v1) supplied over a separately trusted channel. Requires --reference-time. When supplied the evaluation emits key_authentic checking the envelope's producer_key_id against the registry's declared windows. |
| `--registry-signature` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Declared producer-signature envelope JSON (mumei.producer-signature/v1) claiming to sign the --key-registry document's exact bytes. Requires --key-registry. When supplied the evaluation emits registry_signature_bound comparing the wrapper's declared subject_digest to the registry's SHA-256 — representation-level only, no signature verification. |
| `--revocation-signature` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Declared producer-signature envelope JSON (mumei.producer-signature/v1) claiming to sign the --revocation-list document's exact bytes. Requires --revocation-list. When supplied the evaluation emits revocation_signature_bound comparing the wrapper's declared subject_digest to the list's SHA-256 — representation-level only, no signature verification. |
| `--min-revocation-version` | `<N>` | no | — | Declared minimum list_version the revocation list must clear. Requires --revocation-list naming a mumei.key-revocation-list/v2 document, --reference-time and a signed list (--revocation-signature). When supplied the evaluation emits revocation_list_current checking the list's declared window and version. |
| `--reference-time` | `<RFC3339>` | no | — | The caller's declared reference time (RFC 3339 with timezone, e.g. 2026-11-18T00:00:00Z) the registry windows and the envelope's produced_at stamp are compared against. The fold never reads the system clock. Required with --key-registry or --max-age-seconds. |
| `--max-age-seconds` | `<N>` | no | — | Declared freshness window in seconds: the envelope's optional produced_at stamp must be no older than reference_time minus N seconds. Requires --reference-time. When supplied the evaluation emits envelope_fresh. |
| `--output` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Write the evaluation descriptor to PATH instead of stdout. |


## `mumei-agent signature-verify`

Verify a declared producer-signature envelope's ed25519 signature under a declared public key and emit the verification descriptor.

### Options

| Option | Value | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--envelope` | `<PATH>` | yes | — | Declared producer-signature envelope JSON (mumei.producer-signature/v1). |
| `--producer-key` | `<HEX>` | yes | — | Raw ed25519 public key (64-char lowercase hex) supplied over a separately trusted channel. The route verifies the envelope's signature over subject_digest under this key. |
| `--expected-subject` | `<HEX>` | no | — | Declared record digest the signature should cover (64-char lowercase SHA-256 hex). When supplied the verification emits subject_bound comparing it to the envelope's subject_digest. |
| `--expected-producer-key` | `<ID>` | no | — | Declared producer key id the caller trusts, arriving over a separately trusted channel. When supplied the verification emits key_pinned comparing it to the envelope's producer_key_id. |
| `--revocation-list` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Declared revocation list JSON (mumei.key-revocation-list/v1) supplied over a separately trusted channel. When supplied the verification emits key_not_revoked checking the envelope's producer_key_id against the list's revoked_keys. |
| `--key-registry` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Declared producer-key registry JSON (mumei.producer-key-registry/v1) supplied over a separately trusted channel. Requires --reference-time. When supplied the verification emits key_authentic checking the envelope's producer_key_id against the registry's declared windows. |
| `--registry-signature` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Declared producer-signature envelope JSON (mumei.producer-signature/v1) signing the --key-registry document's exact bytes — its subject_digest must be the SHA-256 of those bytes. Requires --key-registry and --registry-key. When supplied the verification emits registry_authentic and ANDs it into key_authentic. |
| `--registry-key` | `<HEX>` | no | — | Raw ed25519 public key (64-char lowercase hex) of the registry's signer — the consumer-pinned root key, supplied over a separately trusted channel. Requires --registry-signature. |
| `--revocation-signature` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Declared producer-signature envelope JSON (mumei.producer-signature/v1) signing the --revocation-list document's exact bytes. Requires --revocation-list and --revocation-key. When supplied the verification emits revocation_list_authentic and ANDs it into key_not_revoked. |
| `--min-revocation-version` | `<N>` | no | — | Declared minimum list_version the revocation list must clear. Requires --revocation-list naming a mumei.key-revocation-list/v2 document, --reference-time and a signed list (--revocation-signature and --revocation-key). When supplied the evaluation emits revocation_list_current checking the list's declared window and version. |
| `--revocation-key` | `<HEX>` | no | — | Raw ed25519 public key (64-char lowercase hex) of the revocation list's signer — the consumer-pinned root key, supplied over a separately trusted channel. Requires --revocation-signature. |
| `--reference-time` | `<RFC3339>` | no | — | The caller's declared reference time (RFC 3339 with timezone, e.g. 2026-11-18T00:00:00Z) the registry windows and the envelope's produced_at stamp are compared against. The fold never reads the system clock. Required with --key-registry or --max-age-seconds. |
| `--max-age-seconds` | `<N>` | no | — | Declared freshness window in seconds: the envelope's optional produced_at stamp must be no older than reference_time minus N seconds. Requires --reference-time. When supplied the evaluation emits envelope_fresh. |
| `--output` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Write the verification descriptor to PATH instead of stdout. |

| `--adapter-overlay` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Declared JSON array of user adapter manifests registered after --adapters; an overlay entry adds a new adapter or replaces the same adapter_id. Repeatable; later overlays win. Manifests are parsed statically; nothing is loaded or executed. |
| `--argv-map` | `<PATH>` | yes | — | Declared JSON object mapping adapter_id to its argv array. |
| `--policy` | `<PATH>` | yes | — | Declared planner policy JSON. allowed_permissions must be declared (an empty list permits only permission-free adapters); optional Boolean require_enforced_isolation defaults to false and fails closed when required isolation or memory cannot be enforced. |
| `--observations` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Optional declared JSON array of runtime observations. |
| `--source` | `<PATH>` | yes | — | Declared .mm source file (absolute path). |
| `--max-attempts` | `<<N>>` | no | 8 | Bounded schedule attempts across all adapters. |
| `--success-exit-code` | `<<N>>` | no | — | Declared exit code counting as a scheduling success (repeatable; default {0}). |
| `--memory-bound-mb` | `<<MB>>` | no | — | Optional declared POSIX RLIMIT_AS ceiling per attempt child. |
| `--core` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Optional Core executable: when a schedule selects an attempt, run the Core representation check on its captured output and record the mumei.evidence-check-acceptance/v1 descriptor. |
| `--core-requirement` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Optional declared mumei.evidence-requirement/v1 document: requires --core; the selected attempt's check becomes the requirement-declared `evidence accept` and the recorded outcome is Core's verdict. |
| `--core-requirement-list` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Optional declared mumei.evidence-requirement-list/v1 document: requires --core and conflicts with --core-requirement; the selected attempt's check becomes the conjunctive requirement-declared `evidence accept` and the descriptor is promotable gate input. |
| `--export-evidence-acceptance` | `<DIR>` | no | — | Optional export directory: requires --core-requirement-list; writes the promotable gate triple (requirement-list.json, evidence.json, acceptance.json) for `mumei claims --require-evidence-acceptance`. |
| `--output` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Write the schedule document here instead of stdout. |
| `--history-log` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Append every plan of the schedule (the initial plan, then each replan, in order) to an opt-in tamper-evident plan history log (mumei.verification-plan-history-entry/v1) as one batch, rolled back on write failure (a killed process can leave a prefix of the batch). Not Evidence, a dispatch record or authentication. |
| `--expected-history-head` | `<HEX>` | no | — | Refuse to append unless the log's last entry digest equals this pinned head. Requires --history-log. |

## `mumei-agent native-object-accept`

Run Core's bounded object-stage machine-code acceptance under an assumed, not validated, register convention and stated input domain. Core's machine_code_entry_wrapper_tv is consumed only when the valid descriptor lists it in checks_performed; when applicable, it checks one unconditional main call to __mumei_user_main returning the low 32 bits of its result. Applicability requires both object symbols and a supported __mumei_user_main source signature. This makes no CRT, loader, OS exit-status, ABI or runtime claim; os_exit_status_observation remains a separate runtime-observation check and is not discharged. This emits no evidence candidate, is not reusable Evidence or a certificate, is not a recovery performer, and does not promote a grade; broader C entry-wrapper behavior, CRT, loader/libc, ABI/runtime, optimizer semantics, producer authenticity and historical execution remain outside the profile. object_translation_correspondence here is only profile-bounded source-to-object machine-code correspondence, not universal object TV. Core's machine_code_f64_scalar_function_tv is consumed only when listed in checks_performed and is limited to Core's f64 profile with XMM argument/result registers assumed, not validated. MXCSR RNE, masked exceptions, FTZ/DAZ-off assumptions and NaN payload bits remain unestablished and not performed; the agent never discharges the external-callee, MXCSR or NaN-payload assumption markers even if a descriptor lists them as performed. Direct-call f64 arguments are admitted only under Core's exact-bits obligation (NaN-aware match, then an exact-bit proof against the XMM argument); computed f64 arguments without provably identical bits and f64 tail calls fail closed. This makes no IEEE-754 conformance, ABI, runtime or full object-TV claim. Core's `machine_code_composite_register_aggregate_tv` is consumed only when listed in `checks_performed`. It covers one- through sixteen-leaf struct parameters and direct-call struct arguments, and struct results of at most four leaves (at most three integer leaves in rax/rdx/rcx and at most two f64 leaves in xmm0/xmm1), with integer and/or f64 leaves; an i128/u128 leaf occupies two consecutive integer slots, low half first. Integer leaves take the next register in rdi–r9 and f64 leaves the next in xmm0–xmm7; leaves without a free register in their class are passed on the argument stack in declaration order, as LLVM lowers scalar stack arguments. Four-integer-leaf results (hidden sret) and three-f64-leaf results (x87) fail closed. One- and two-leaf values use Core's existing assumed SysV eightbyte convention; aggregates wider than two leaves assume LLVM first-class aggregate lowering, not SysV C-ABI classification, and `machine_code_tv_sysv_memory_class_aggregate_abi` stays not performed. This makes no ABI, runtime or full object-TV claim.

### Options

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--core` | `<PATH>` | yes | — | Declared Core executable (absolute path) used to run `native-bundle accept-object`. |
| `--bundle` | `<DIR>` | yes | — | Declared native-bundle directory (absolute path) holding native-bundle.json and its declared members. |
| `--source` | `<PATH>` | yes | — | Declared caller-supplied .mm source (absolute path, at most 65536 bytes); the bundle's own labels/paths are never read. |
| `--expected-build-id` | `<SHA256>` | yes | — | SHA-256 of native-bundle.json obtained through a separately trusted channel. |
| `--attempt-timeout` | `<<MS>>` | no | 60000 | Declared attempt bound in milliseconds. |
| `--memory-bound-mb` | `<<MB>>` | no | — | Optional declared POSIX RLIMIT_AS ceiling applied to the attempt child's whole address space. |
| `--output` | `<PATH>` | no | — | Write the object-accept report JSON here instead of stdout. |

## `mumei-agent rust-summaries`

Emit opt-in Rust interprocedural dependency summaries as JSON — a conservative report, not a proof or verdict.

### Positional arguments

| Argument | Required | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | yes | `<SOURCE>` | Path to a single Rust source file (at most 64 KiB). |

### Options

| Option | Value | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--resolve-modules` | — | no | — | Resolve `mod NAME;` declarations from the importer's directory (`<dir>/NAME.rs`, `<dir>/NAME/mod.rs`); unresolved declarations stay opaque. |
| `--summary-aware-calls` | `<<MANIFEST>>` | no | — | Callee summary manifest (mumei.rust-scalar-parameter-deps/v1): an opaque call whose recorded name a manifest entry covers folds the entry's declared return_dependencies instead of the opaque every-argument union. The manifest is trusted as declared; its canonical bytes fold into the context key. |

|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | yes | `<SOURCE>` | Path to a single Rust source file (at most 64 KiB). |

### Options

| Option | Value | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|

The manifest is trusted as declared; its canonical bytes fold into the context key. |
| `--manifest` | `<<PATH>>` | yes | — | Summary manifest (mumei.rust-scalar-parameter-deps/v1) to accept from. |
| `--function` | `<<NAME>>` | yes | — | Function whose summary to accept — the emitted name or a bare member name when it is unambiguous. Accepted only when the manifest's context key still matches the fresh derivation and the function survives in it. |

| Argument | Required | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source_file` | no | `[<SOURCE_FILE>]` | Path to a .mm source file or directory to heal (default: examples/sword_test.mm). Directories are searched recursively and processed in dependency-first order; runtime may exceed N× single-file healing due to dependency resolution. |

### Options

| Option | Value | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--max-retries` | `<MAX_RETRIES>` | no | — | Maximum number of fix attempts (default: from config or 5) |
| `--strategy` | `{single, multi-stage}` | no | — | Fix strategy: 'single' (one-shot) or 'multi-stage' (diagnose→fix→validate). Default: from AGENT_STRATEGY env var or 'single'. |
| `--generate` | `<SPEC_JSON>` | no | — | Generate mode: path to a JSON spec file describing the atom to generate. Runs generate → verify → fix loop instead of the normal heal loop. |
| `--output` | `<OUTPUT_FILE>` | no | — | Output file for generated code (required with --generate). |
| `--budget-policy` | `<POLICY_JSON>` | no | — | Path to retry budget policy JSON (default: built-in P8-G policy). |
| `--proof-cert-out` | `<CERT_JSON>` | no | — | After healing, emit a proof certificate for the final source with the repair outcome attached as self_correction_metadata (input for mumei benchmarks/evaluation_suite.py --repair-cert-dir). When SOURCE is a directory this is a directory too: each file gets <dir>/<relative path>.proof.json. |
| `--charter-lock` | `<LOCK_JSON>` | no | — | Use this charter lock instead of discovering one from the source tree. |
| `--allow-contract-erosion` | — | no | — | Disable contract-erosion checks for repair candidates. |
| `--controls-gate` | `{off, warn, require}` | no | off | Rank verified heal candidates using negative controls (default: off). |
